message: Bump to v0.15.1

CodeTab: preview images instead of rendering bytes as text Selecting an image in the code viewer now shows the image rather than its raw bytes in Monaco. - /api/files/read classifies raster image extensions as language "image" and returns empty content (skips reading binary as UTF-8 + the 5MB text cap), reporting the file size instead. - New /api/files/raw streams file bytes with the correct Content-Type, reusing read's project-path validation. Used as the source. - CodeTab renders an inline image pane (centered, contained, with pixel dimensions) for raster images, and a click-to-zoom that reuses the existing ImagePreview modal. SVG keeps an Edit/Preview toggle: Preview renders the image, Edit shows the XML source in Monaco.
Commit leftover changes for: Fast dragging bottom window loses position

PanelGrid: disable iframe/webview pointer events during lower-panel drag

Fast-dragging the lower panel's sub-nav over an iframe or <webview>
(e.g. an open Live panel above) stalled the drag because raw mouse
handlers don't get pointer capture — the embed swallowed the
mousemove events. Match the pattern already used in LiveTab's viewport
resize: zero out pointer-events on all iframes/webviews for the
duration of the drag, restore on mouseup.
Bump to v0.15.0

AgentInputBar: add terminal-style Up/Down history navigation

Up recalls the previous sent message when the input is empty, like a
terminal. Once navigating, further Up walks back, Down walks forward,
and Down past the newest clears the input. Typing exits history mode.

History is in-memory per mount (consecutive duplicates collapsed).
Sent text is pushed in all three send paths: normal send, immediate
interrupt, and confirmed interrupt.

LiveTab: move Clear site data dropdown right of URL bar

LiveTab: add Clear site data dropdown (Electron only)

Eraser icon next to the refresh button opens a dropdown with three
options: Clear Local Storage (+sessionStorage), Clear Cookies, or
Clear Everything. Each calls a new webview:clear-storage IPC handler

Add whitespace-nowrap so the buttons don't wrap to two lines and grow
taller than neighbouring controls when the code panel gets narrow.
Bump to v0.14.4

LiveTab: drop "start the server" subheading from empty state

Divider "or" alone is enough — the three buttons speak for themselves.

LiveTab: add "File" empty-state option that loads local files via file://

Adds a native file picker (osascript) as a third option alongside Agent/Terminal,
wraps the picked path in a file:// URL, and reworks the empty-state copy:
"Connect to a running server" / "or" / "start the server".

Bare absolute paths typed into the URL inputs are auto-wrapped in file:// too,
and the toolbar URL bar now handles "/foo" navigation correctly when the
current serverUrl is file:// (file URL origins resolve to "null" and break
naive base+path concatenation).

Directory listings (e.g. file:///Users/brian/Desktop/) render via Chromium's
built-in directory index — no extra work needed. Desktop-only in practice;
plain browsers block file:// in iframes for security.
Bump to v0.14.3

usePanelLayout: self-heal poisoned lower.sizePct on upper re-show

If the user is stuck in the legacy state where lower.sizePct was persisted at ~100 (upper row hidden), simply toggling an upper slot back on would render upper as a sliver and immediately re-trip the snap-close threshold. Reset lower.sizePct to default when transitioning from "upper fully hidden" to "upper visible" if the saved value is unreasonably high (>90).

PanelGrid: don't persist lower.sizePct when only Lower is visible

When the upper row is hidden, react-resizable-panels reports lower.sizePct=100 (the panel fills the group). Persisting that poisons the lower/upper share so re-opening UL/UR computes upperSizePct=~0, which trips the snap-close threshold and re-hides the panel on the next layout-changed callback. The user gets stuck unable to reopen any panel.

CodeTab: show gitignored files in tree by default

Default `showHidden` to true so files like `.env.local` are visible in the
file tree without having to discover the eye toggle. Gitignored files still
render with opacity-50 to distinguish them from tracked files, and the
toggle remains for hiding them. Existing user preferences (saved as '0' or
'1' in localStorage) are respected; only the absent-preference default flips.

AskQuestionBlock: add synthetic "Other" option that reveals a free-text input

The AskUserQuestion tool documents that an "Other" choice is always available, but the UI didn't render one. Append a dashed "Other" tile to each question's options. In single-question mode it activates a textarea + Send button (Enter submits); in multi-question mode it toggles like any other option, and Submit uses the typed text as that question's answer (skipped if empty).
CommitModal: drop "Almost there..." stage and stay on "Generating commit message..." until LLM responds

Fix app failing to relaunch after web update

When "Restart to update" is clicked for a web-only update, the relaunch
took the `relaunch` exit path: enterExiting awaited stopServer(), then
called app.relaunch() + app.exit(0). But stopServer can take >3s when
`npm run start` ignores SIGTERM and waits for the SIGKILL fallback, so
the 3s exit watchdog fired process.exit(0) first — bypassing Electron's
Shutdown entirely and dropping the queued relaunch flag.

Two changes:
- Call app.relaunch() before the await, so the flag is set even when the
  watchdog wins the race.
- Watchdog now uses app.exit(0) instead of process.exit(0), so Shutdown
  runs and honors the relaunch flag (spawns the relaunch helper).
Bump to v0.14.2

LiveTab: persist liveUrl/liveViewport so the URL bar survives reloads

updateProject silently dropped these fields, so PATCHes from the
debounced URL persist (fired on each webview did-navigate event) never
landed in workspace.json. The bar always re-rendered with serverUrl on
panel toggles and page reloads.

Also flush a pending persist on unmount via fetch keepalive so a quick
panel-switch within the 500ms debounce doesn't lose the most recent URL.

StatusBlock: show session ID after model name on init

Enrich the existing init block with sessionId once Claude CLI emits its
system init event, then re-broadcast so live viewers update in place.
Clients dedup status:init by timestamp.
Bump to v0.14.1

PanelGrid: bump lower panel snap-close threshold to 88px

The lower panel sub-nav is taller than the L/R divider area, so 64px
let users leave a barely-visible sliver. Bump the lower-specific
threshold to 88px while leaving the L/R and upper-row snap-close at 64.
StatusBlock: place timestamp right after duration in complete divider

AskQuestionBlock: render option preview text statically

The `preview` field on AskUserQuestion options was being stripped by the
type cast at the two callsites and never declared on QuestionOption, so
agents who provided previews had them silently dropped. Surface previews
beneath each option as a mono-font block; switch to a vertical stack
when any option has a preview so it gets full width.

KanbanPanelView: scope file-drop overlay to the kanban panel

The "Drop to create new task" overlay used to live on the page's <main>
wrapper, covering the entire panel grid at z-40. With workbench/live
panels visible alongside kanban, the overlay swallowed any file drag
intended for the workbench's chat input — so dragging an image into
the chat created a new task instead.

Move the file-drop handlers and overlay into KanbanPanelView so they
only activate over the kanban panel itself. Workbench drops now reach
AgentInputBar normally.

PanelGrid: reset library layout cache on snap-close

When a panel was dragged below the snap-close threshold, the library
cached the tiny drag-end size against the current panel-id set. Toggling
the panel back on rehydrated from that cache instead of our defaultLayout
prop, so the panel reappeared at near-zero pixels and looked closed
until a hard refresh reset the cache.

Force the cache to a usable size via the imperative setLayout API
before flipping visible to false, in all three snap-close paths
(sub-nav drag, outer divider for lower or upper row, inner divider
for L/R).

MermaidDiagram: scale SVG to fill container width

Mermaid emits SVGs with inline `style="max-width: <intrinsic>px"`,
which capped tiny diagrams at their native width and left a wide
panel mostly empty. Override with `[&_svg]:!max-w-full` so the
SVG scales up via its viewBox — text and nodes scale
proportionally instead of sitting cramped at intrinsic size.

Markdown: render mermaid fenced blocks as diagrams

Adds a shared MermaidDiagram component (lazy-loaded mermaid v11,
theme-aware via the existing MutationObserver pattern, debounced
~150ms with error fallback to raw code).

Hooked into the `pre` override of all three markdown render sites
so the diagram replaces the styled-pre wrapper:
  - blocks/TextBlock.tsx (chat / agent text)
  - TaskAgentDetail.tsx mdComponents (task descriptions + summaries)
  - CodeTab.tsx markdown preview

commit_changes: stop auto-staging; agent controls `git add`

The MCP tool used to run `git add -A` before committing, which swept up
changes from other tasks running in the same working tree. Now it only
runs `git commit -m` — the agent stages with `git add <files>` first.
If nothing is staged, the tool errors with a hint telling the agent to
stage the files it changed (and to avoid `git add -A`).

Mirrored the same change on the workbench-side `commit_changes`
(proq-mcp-project.js + agent-tab-runtime.ts), since the bleed risk is
the same on a shared project dir.

Restored the "commit after each logical unit of work" guidance in the
task-agent prompt, framed around the agent's own files: stage only what
**you** changed, then commit; before completing the task, make sure all
of your work is committed.

Task Agent: stop pushing reflexive auto-commits

Replace "commit after each logical unit of work / always commit before
reporting / don't leave uncommitted work behind" in the task-agent
system prompt with a single "commit before completing the task"
instruction. Same softening on the `commit_changes` tool description.

Aggressive nudges combined with `git add -A` were causing agents to
sweep in changes that belonged to a different in-progress task.

Agents: add mcp__proq__sleep + Waiting & monitoring prompt nudge

New `sleep` MCP tool registers a wakeup, returns immediately, and re-enters
this exact session via continueSession() with --resume when the timer fires.
Backed by a per-task pendingWait field on the Task row so wakeups survive
proq restarts (bootstrap on module init re-arms timers).

System prompt now steers agents toward Bash run_in_background + Monitor for
process output, sleep for long timed polling, and explicitly away from
ScheduleWakeup / CronCreate (which don't continue the session).

Manual followup/interrupt and abortTask both cancel any pending wait, so
human input always pre-empts an automated wakeup.

Agent chat divider: append hh:mm timestamp to completion divider

Show a short local time stamp on the right of the completed-session

Bump to v0.14.0
Task agent subnav: show short task ID in grey on the right

Panels: snap closed when dragged below 64px, reopen at default size

Drop minSize on all panels and the custom lower-resize clamp so dragging
can cross the snap threshold. On drag release (both react-resizable-panels'
onLayoutChanged and the custom sub-nav drag), measure the panel's pixel
size against SNAP_CLOSE_PX=64 and either persist the new sizePct or hide
the slot and reset its sizePct to the layout default — so toggling it
back on via the TopBar lands at a usable size.

Lower panel resize: force grabbing cursor with !important style during drag

The previous body-cursor approach lost to the sub-nav div's own
`cursor-grab` class whenever the pointer was over that div. Inject a
temporary <style> element with `* { cursor: grabbing !important }` for
the duration of the drag so every element shows the grabbing cursor
regardless of its own cursor rule. Removed on mouseup.

Lower panel resize: pin grab point to cursor (no edge-snap jump)

Instead of mapping the cursor's absolute Y to the divider position
(which yanks the toolbar to the top so the edge meets the cursor on
mousedown), capture the initial cursor Y and lower panel size, then
adjust the size by the cursor's *displacement* during the drag. The
spot the user grabbed stays pinned under the cursor.

Lower panel resize: force body cursor to grabbing during drag

Tailwind's :active pseudo-class is unreliable while dragging because
mouse events go to a window-level listener, not the original element.
Set document.body.style.cursor = 'grabbing' (and userSelect = 'none' to
prevent text selection flashes) for the duration of the drag, then
restore both on mouseup.

In-app image preview: shared lightbox with trackpad zoom/pan

Adds a reusable ImagePreview component (black overlay, click-to-close,
Escape, trackpad pinch-zoom toward cursor, two-finger pan when zoomed,
double-click to reset). Replaces the per-place window.open behavior so
all clickable image thumbnails now preview in-app:

- UserBlock (already had an inline lightbox; consolidated onto the shared one)
- AgentInputBar attachment chips
- TaskAgentDetail task attachments
- TaskDraft attachment chips (image only — non-image files keep their tab open)
- Supervisor page input attachments
Commit leftover changes for: New Panels and Panel Bars Complete

Live & Code panels: render toolbar into PanelChrome subnav

Both views previously stacked their own h-10 toolbar below the panel
chrome row, leaving the chrome row mostly empty. PanelChrome now exposes
its subnav slot via context (usePanelSubnavSlot); LiveTab and CodeTab
portal their existing toolbars into that slot, matching how Kanban and
Workbench already use subnavContent.

Lower panel sub-nav: grab cursor on background, keep resize on edge

The empty area of the lower panel's sub-nav now shows the grab cursor
(grabbing while dragging) so it reads as "drag this region" rather than
"row-resize." The PanelSeparator edge between upper/lower keeps its
existing cursor-row-resize affordance.

desktop: harden shell auto-update against stuck-shell scenarios

Five fixes that together make sure users stuck on a buggy shell version
escape on the next launch and don't get re-stuck.

1. Single-instance lock. A second .app launch (double-click, dock
   activation while splash is still up) used to spawn a competing
   process — multiple shells racing on git pull / npm install was the
   root of the "spawned a bunch of them" failure. Now the second launch
   focuses the existing window.

2. Boot-time orphan-update rescue. If a previous session downloaded an
   update but never installed it (broken in-app restart, hung quit,
   force-quit before autoInstallOnAppQuit fired), we re-trigger the
   electron-updater flow on launch. checkForUpdates discovers the cached
   download, fires update-downloaded immediately, we quitAndInstall.
   Times out at 12s so a network-down boot doesn't stall.

3. Watchdog skips install-shell-update. enterExiting's 3s
   process.exit(0) was killing quitAndInstall mid-install — extracting
   the .zip and swapping the .app bundle legitimately runs longer than
   3s. Skip the watchdog for that reason; quit/relaunch keep it.

4. isShellUpdateDownloaded() also returns true when a cached download
   from a previous session exists for a newer version. Previously it
   only reflected the in-session update-downloaded event, so the in-app
   "Restart to update" button was hidden for stale downloads.

5. Sidebar settings badge lights up on shell-update:downloaded too, not
   just the web-update channel.

Lower panel sub-nav resize: ignore clicks via interactive-ancestor check

The previous `e.target === e.currentTarget` gate broke whenever a view's
subnav wrapped its content in its own flex-1 div (Workbench, Kanban) —
clicks on the visually-empty area landed on the view's wrapper, not on
PanelChrome's wrapper, so the resize never started.

Replace the strict-equality check with a `closest()` interactive-ancestor
filter so non-interactive descendants (view wrapper divs) are treated as
empty space, while clicks on tabs, buttons, etc. still pass through.

Reconcile project queues on WS server boot

Iterates all projects after the WS server starts listening and calls

agentStatus="running" rows where the live session is gone, so this

Bump to v0.12.0

Scrub NODE_ENV from agent/shell child process envs

Electron sets NODE_ENV=production on the host, which leaked through the
Next.js server into every spawned Claude Code agent and PTY shell. That
broke Vite dev servers run from those shells — @vitejs/plugin-react v6
reads config.isProduction in configResolved, disabling Fast Refresh, so
OXC-emitted $RefreshReg$/$RefreshSig$ references crash hydration with
ReferenceError.

Consolidate the child-env construction (which was duplicated at 9 spawn
sites) into a single childProcessEnv() helper in utils.ts that strips
NODE_ENV, CLAUDECODE, and PORT. Apply it across agent-dispatch,
agent-session, agent-tab-runtime, supervisor-runtime, pty-server,
claude-cli, and proq-bridge.
Bump to v0.11.8

Make proq MCP tool schemas strict so unknown args fail validation

Every `server.tool(name, desc, shape, handler)` call in proq-mcp-task.js
and proq-mcp-project.js was passing a raw shape object, which the SDK
internally wrapped with a non-strict `z.object(shape)` — silently
dropping unknown keys. Agents calling e.g. `create_task({ status:
"in-progress" })` would see the task land in todo with no indication
the `status` field had been ignored.

Switch every tool to `server.registerTool(name, { description,
inputSchema: z.object(shape).strict() }, handler)`. `registerTool`
accepts a pre-built ZodObject (the legacy `tool()` overload
misidentifies a ZodObject as annotations), and a strict object rejects
unknown keys with a zod `unrecognized_keys` error that names the
offending field. Advertised JSON schemas now include
`additionalProperties: false` so clients know the shape.

No tool names, descriptions, or field definitions changed.

Wire --chrome flag into workbench agent tab sessions

Workbench agent tabs now honor settings.useChrome like task agents do.
When enabled, spawns Claude CLI with --chrome and allows
mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools. Extracted buildAllowedTools helper to
avoid duplicating the literal tool list across the two spawn sites
(startAgentTabSession and continueAgentTabSession).

next: externalize chokidar and fsevents for server bundle

app.relaunch() in dev mode loses ELECTRON_RENDERER_URL — electron-vite only
sets it on the original spawn — so the wizard window in the relaunched process
loaded nothing and just sat black until the dev server was killed and restarted.

Switch Reset to a `running → setup` transition handled entirely in-process.
exitState now also stops the health monitor, schedulers, and the server when
the next state is `setup`, so the wizard re-enters server-less. enterSetup
already destroys lingering windows and creates a fresh wizard.

Production behavior is unchanged in spirit — the wizard still ends up running
against a clean config — without paying the dev-mode cost.

Migrate legacy slug-named agent files to {id}.json

Commit 902a22d4 switched agent file storage from {slug}.json to
{id}.json but didn't rename existing files, so getAgent/updateAgent
silently returned null for any pre-existing agent. The UI listed
agents fine (directory scan) but edits no-op'd on a 404.

desktop: broadcast app-state:changed and show renderer overlay

Main process registers an onStateChange listener that broadcasts the new state
to every BrowserWindow over a new app-state:changed IPC channel. The renderer
exposes it via window.proqDesktop.onAppStateChanged in preload, and a new
AppStateOverlay component mounted alongside ShellInner displays:

- "Restarting…" when state is exiting/relaunch
- "Installing update…" when state is exiting/install-shell-update
- "Quitting…" when state is exiting/quit
- "Reconnecting…" when state is recovering

Gives the user immediate feedback for transitions that previously looked like
the app had frozen.

desktop: route every entry point through state machine

Redesign queue: liveness-first, drop "starting" state, CLI exit handler

processQueue no longer trusts the denormalized agentStatus field to decide
what's running — the field lags DB writes and drifts across restarts.
Instead it asks isSessionAlive(taskId) for every in-progress task; that's
the actual process/session, so ordering bugs and unclean exits can't
confuse it.

by the per-project re-entrancy guard. A task is now either running

Fix restart-to-update button hanging due to stopServer() never resolving

The root cause: stopServer() listened for the 'close' event on the npm
child process. In Node.js, 'close' only fires when the process exits
AND all stdio streams are closed. But npm spawns `next start` as a
grandchild that inherits the piped stdout/stderr — when SIGTERM kills
npm, the grandchild keeps those pipes open, so 'close' never fires.
The Promise never resolves, `app.exit(0)` is never reached, and the
button appears to do nothing.

Two fixes:
1. stopServer(): use 'exit' event instead of 'close' — 'exit' fires
   when the process dies regardless of stdio stream state.
2. app:restart handler: don't await stopServer() at all. Just relaunch
   and exit immediately — startServer() already kills stale port
   processes on boot. Added process.exit(0) fallback in case app.exit()
   is deferred by the event loop.

Optimistically show thinking indicator and stop button on follow-up send

When the user sends a follow-up, there was a round-trip delay before

Fix active state not updating: set session.status before broadcasting

Two bugs in agent-session.ts:

1. processStreamEvent result handler called appendBlock() before setting

   agent finished — stop button stayed visible and non-functional.

   active: true broadcast came after an async getSettings() call,
   creating a gap where the thinking indicator wouldn't show.

Fix: set session.status before appendBlock in both cases. The user block
now carries active: true immediately, and the completion block carries
active: false.

Fix frontend staleness: globalThis singletons + await processQueue

Two root causes of UI falling out of sync with API:

1. lowdb singletons (db instances, write locks) and agent-dispatch
   state (cleanup timers, processing guard) were module-level variables
   that got destroyed on Next.js HMR. Detached processQueue() calls
   would write to orphaned instances invisible to new request handlers.
   Fix: attach all singletons to globalThis so they survive HMR.

2. processQueue() was fire-and-forget in PATCH and reorder routes,
   so responses returned before dispatch state transitions completed.
   Frontend polls would see stale dispatch state.
   Fix: await processQueue, re-read task for fresh state in response.
